questions.text: What does freedom of speech mean in Australia?
options: People may express ideas within the law
Only elected officials may speak publicly
Newspapers must agree with the government
questions.explanation: People in Australia may express their ideas freely, provided they remain within the law.

questions.text: Which statement reflects equality in Australia?
options: Men and women have equal rights
A person's wealth determines their rights
Only citizens must obey the law
Some religions have greater legal rights
questions.explanation: Australian law gives men and women equal rights.

questions.text: What is an example of mutual respect?
options: Listening to views you disagree with
questions.explanation: Australians are expected to respect the rights and opinions of others, even when they disagree.

questions.text: Is violence acceptable when people disagree?
options: No, disagreement should be resolved peacefully
Yes, if the issue is important
questions.explanation: Violence is not accepted as a way to change a person's mind or the law.

questions.text: Who makes and changes federal laws in Australia?
questions.explanation: The Australian Parliament makes and changes federal laws.

questions.text: What are the two houses of the Australian Parliament?
options: The Senate and the House of Representatives
The Cabinet and the High Court
The police and the Defence Force
questions.explanation: The Australian Parliament consists of the King, the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.text: Who is Australia's Head of State?
questions.explanation: The King of Australia is Australia's Head of State and is represented federally by the Governor-General.

questions.text: Voting in federal elections is compulsory for Australian citizens aged 18 or over. Is this true?
options: Only for people who own property
questions.explanation: Australian citizens aged 18 years or over must enrol and vote in federal elections and referenda.

options: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
questions.explanation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are Australia's first inhabitants.
Australia Day is celebrated on 26 January each year.

The opening of the first Parliament House
The arrival of the First Fleet only
questions.explanation: Anzac Day commemorates all Australians and New Zealanders who served and died in wars, conflicts and peacekeeping operations.

questions.text: When did the separate colonies unite in a federation of states?
questions.explanation: On 1 January 1901, the colonies united into a federation called the Commonwealth of Australia.
